data.turoyo: Omər: "Ṣrəṭləx gawi." Ummo: "Gḥayṭalle gawox, gmanəḥallox." Omər: "E."

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/108)

data.turoyo: Ayna d̥kə́twalle ṣaʕro zewudo, ḥəyewən, ʕeze, saymiwa maršo xano. Hano ḥəšwínale maršo manək, ṣaʕro, as+sappoṯayḏe maqimíwanne, ḥayṭiwa u+rešawo ŭ hawo, howewa bu+šəkl dəmmat yani du+qawro, kiban dəmmina xud u+qawro d̥owe ḥfiro, ḥa d̥ḥofar qawro. <...>
data.translation: Whoever had extra hair, animals, goats, would make a carpet like this one. This one, let’s consider it one of those carpets, hair, they would raise its edges, they would sow on top of that one (lit. ‘that head’) and that one, it would turn into the shape, you might say, like, of a grave, we could say like a grave that is excavated, as if someone digs a grave. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell; making a carpet bag identifies the two ends being sewn. Edition sow is retained verbatim.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (JTM 2.4/5)

data.turoyo: I qabrəġaye annaqla, lə kubʕewola ḥayṭo ste, kit hən mena arbaʕ, arbaʕ darzat mi xaṣrayo w mayo, kətwo hawxa əmmiwola mḥaṭo rabṯo, msalle, suxriwola.
data.translation: Die qabrəġaye brauchte man nicht einmal zuzunähen. Manche mussten aber mit vier Nähten auf jeder Seite geschlossen werden. Es gab (dafür) eine große Nadel, die wir msalle (Sacknadel) nannten.

rationale: Thin inherited Detransitive Infinitiv cell; verbal sewing noun in a requirement construction, not feminine finite ḥayṭo or thread.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (52/10)

data.turoyo: Ḥzele, ga kale komfaṣəl u qumaš w mḥaḏ̣alle l ḥyoṭo w naqqa ḥreto komoyəd laf falqanək, mqaṣqaṣṣe w mḥalaqqe l tamo.
data.translation: Er traf ihn an, wie er Stoff zuschnitt und für das Nähen herrichtete. Dann aber nahm er die zugeschnittenen Teile, zerstückelte sie und warf sie weg.

rationale: Third inherited Detransitive Infinitiv example; purpose l ḥyoṭo and source vocalism contrast with ḥayṭo, without inferring a semantically Detransitive event.

summary: All 25 supplied records were reviewed, including one uninflected false start. The surviving ḥayṭ... fragment is not expanded to an invented complete Infectum form.
Active sewing has unmarked material/patient nouns or object suffixes; b- can introduce a support on which ornaments are sewn, an instrument, or a location. These roles are kept distinct.
The stomach recipe contrasts sewing pieces into pouches and sewing filled pouches shut. Surgical stitching was already in the entry, so neither body tissue nor edible material requires a new sense.

Finite feminine ḥayṭo at the window differs from action noun ḥayṭo in the requirement construction and purpose variant ḥyoṭo. The glossary files the latter under Detransitive Infinitiv; that convention does not itself make the action noun semantically Detransitive.

Detransitive Preterit has a garment patient and needle instrument without an expressed sewer. The inherited negative Detransitive Infectum at 9/22 expresses repairability, not merely an absent action.
MAC Material culture/108 has edition sow where the context is sewing; MAC TERTO ZARE/57 has source -wayna beside English they used to sew. Neither translation is repaired or replaced.

The Hors 1/49 operation noun aʕmayye differs from inherited EL 49 ʕamaliye. Old prs page/line citations recur under supplied PrS text/verse references; these parallels require reconciliation, not silent source replacement.
No new idiom or light-verb sense is established. Adjacent saym/mḥe verbs provide context, but this assignment concerns ḥyṭ occurrences only.
Compare Hors 1/49 aʕmayye with inherited EL 49 ʕamaliye and verify ḥiṭənne segmentation; no silent correction of the surgery quotation was made.
Confirm first-person feminine/object contraction Gḥayṭalle in PrS 34/62.
In MAC Old lady and a bird/30 can ḥəṭle mean fastening beyond sewing, or is English tied a loose rendering? Later explicit sewed favours the ordinary sewing analysis.
In that tale, does -o in ḥiṭole resume the saddlebag, or the dog as enclosed content?
Confirm the person/suffix analysis of ḥayṭənwanne in MAC Famine/59 against the edition's those would sew, and the first-person -wayna versus English they at TERTO ZARE/57.
Reconcile inherited prs 40/29,106/19,109/18,211/8 with supplied PrS 17/44,39/52,40/30,73/42 without conflating numbering systems.
Does Detransitive Infinitiv consistently serve as the glossary's location for active sewing event nouns? Preserve its heading until the team's convention is confirmed.
Is ḥyoṭo at 52/10 a dialect vocalism or a transcription variant of ḥayṭo?

Literal sewing applies to surgical body tissue, edible stomach pouches, garment layers, bag ends and objects attached to a tail. Material and closure result do not establish separate technical or fastening senses.
